judgment.reason: It does not ensure that the chosen family {q_p} leaves any primes available for the r_n. An arbitrary injective assignment indexed by all primes can exhaust all primes, so the asserted selection of r_n outside that family is unsupported.
The proof assumes, without constructing or requiring it, that the q_p-family has infinitely many primes outside it. Pairwise distinct q_p indexed by primes may comprise every prime.
It leaves unjustified the existence of private primes disjoint from the entire preselected q_p-family; that family could equal the set of all primes.
It explicitly chooses two disjoint infinite families of distinct primes, then the recursive size choice ensures monotonicity and the factorization exactly preserves common-prime counts.
